name: nexus-sphere-mcp

tools.name: deliberate
tools.description: Put a judgement call to a council of independent AI models from different vendors (e.g. Claude, GPT, Gemini). Each answers on its own, rebuts the most divergent peer, and a synthesis returns: conclusion, where they agree, where they disagree, each AI's position, and cited web sources. Use for architecture choices, trade-offs, risky decisions and fact-sensitive questions — not for generating code. Takes 1-3 minutes and counts as one AI Meeting against the user's Nexus plan.

question.description: The question, with the options you are weighing.

context.description: Background, constraints or a code snippet the AIs need. Only what you put here is sent — no files are read. Keep it to the relevant part.

participants.description: Preferred AI providers, e.g. ["claude", "openai", "gemini"]. They get seats first; the rest are filled from the providers the user's organisation has enabled.

web_search.description: auto: search when the question needs current facts. on: always. off: never. Sources are cited as [n].

mode.description: quick is faster and cheaper; deep takes longer and argues more.

tools.name: second_opinion
tools.description: Have several independent AI models critique an answer, plan or fix that YOU (the calling agent) produced, before you act on it. They name errors, risky assumptions and better alternatives, say what is right, and each gives a verdict (adopt / adopt with conditions / do not adopt). Returns the consensus, disagreements and sources. Use it when the stakes are high or you are unsure. Takes 1-3 minutes; counts as one AI Meeting.

proposal.description: Your proposed answer / plan / patch summary, exactly as you would present it.

question.description: What the user asked for (so the critics judge against the real goal).

context.description: Background, constraints or a code snippet the AIs need. Only what you put here is sent — no files are read. Keep it to the relevant part.

participants.description: Preferred AI providers, e.g. ["claude", "openai", "gemini"]. They get seats first; the rest are filled from the providers the user's organisation has enabled.

web_search.description: auto: search when the question needs current facts. on: always. off: never. Sources are cited as [n].

mode.description: quick is faster and cheaper; deep takes longer and argues more.

tools.name: review_diff
tools.description: Review a code change with several AI models before it is pushed. Pass a unified diff as `diff` (or per-file `files`). Set source="git" ONLY when the user asked to review this repository's current changes — it then reads `git diff` in the working directory. Returns a risk level (low/medium/high), blocking findings split into agreed vs dissent, per-provider verdicts, and exactly what the council could not see.

source.description: input: review the diff/files passed here. git: read this repository's changes.

working_tree.description: source=git: review uncommitted changes against HEAD instead of the branch diff.

description.description: What the change is meant to do.

tools.name: get_result
tools.description: Fetch the result of a deliberate / second_opinion / review_diff call that was still running when the previous call returned. Does not start a new AI Meeting and costs nothing.

trace_id.description: The trace_id from the earlier call.

instructions: Nexus runs an AI Meeting: several AI models from different vendors answer independently, rebut each other and a synthesis reports agreement, disagreement and sources. Use `second_opinion` to have your own proposed answer or plan critiqued before acting on it, `deliberate` for judgement calls, and `review_diff` before pushing a change. Each call takes 1-3 minutes and uses one AI Meeting from the user's plan, so call it when the stakes justify it, not for every step. When a call returns a trace_id that is still running, call `get_result` later instead of asking again. Tell the user where the AIs disagreed and what the council could not see.
